statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-5545: libcurl can wrongly reuse a connection that was authenticated with HTTP Negotiate for a later request to the same host that uses different credentials (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-5545.html). It affects curl 7.10.6 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/33e43985b8f3b9e66691d06e70be0395849856cd, which makes the connection-reuse match in lib/url.c also check the Negotiate authentication state; that check is compiled only when curl is built with SPNEGO (GSS-API) support. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 main repository publishes curl builds 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. None of them is built with GSS-API or SPNEGO support, on x86_64 or aarch64: none of the libraries libcurl links in any build is a GSS-API or Kerberos library, the strings 'SPNEGO' and 'GSS-API' do not occur in libcurl, the connection structure in the debug information shipped in curl-dbg has no Negotiate state member, and in the static libcurl.a shipped in curl-static the objects built from http_negotiate.c, spnego_gssapi.c, krb5_gssapi.c and curl_gssapi.c define no functions in any build, while the same search finds the functions of the object built from openssl.c in every build. Without Negotiate support a Negotiate-authenticated connection cannot be made, and the code the fix changes is not compiled, so the vulnerable code is not present in any published build.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-5545: libcurl can wrongly reuse a connection that was authenticated with HTTP Negotiate for a later request to the same host that uses different credentials (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-5545.html). It affects curl 7.10.6 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/33e43985b8f3b9e66691d06e70be0395849856cd, which makes the connection-reuse match in lib/url.c also check the Negotiate authentication state; that check is compiled only when curl is built with SPNEGO (GSS-API) support. Debian backported the fix to trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-5545). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64, all later than 8.14.1-2+deb13u4, and each ships a Debian changelog that records the fix under 8.14.1-2+deb13u4. Debian builds curl with GSS-API, so the Negotiate code is present: libcurl.so.4.8.0 and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 link libgssapi_krb5.so.2 in all three builds. In the amd64 libcurl4t64 package of all three builds, the connection-match code checks the Negotiate state directly after the NTLM state, as the fixed code does, which Debian's own unfixed 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 libcurl4t64 build (amd64) does not do. Every published build carries the fix, so the fixed version is the lowest published one, the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5.
